Primary asks:
- Can you provide a clear perf-per-dollar comparison for A100 vs H100 and L40S given our workload (see bullets below)?
- Can Redwood commit to throughput guarantees for the expanded pool (p95 latency targets and throughput per-card)?
- What would the pricing delta look like for a 12-month reserved term with +8 GPUs?

Workload snapshot (ask from infra):
- Model family: mix of instruct + reranking; typical sequence length ~ 512 tokens
- Peak concurrent requests: ~420 concurrent sessions (steady), bursts to ~700
- Average tokens/sec per request: ~30 (varies)
- Latency target: p95 < 250ms for generation up to 512 tokens

Please loop in engineering if you need more telemetry. We want a performance-backed recommendation (not just list prices) to present to procurement.

3) Draft an addendum for your renewal that covers +8 GPUs, target throughput SLAs, and fallback policies (e.g., automatic spill to L40S if H100 capacity constrained).

Prelim numbers (very rough, based on similar customers and average seq len ~512):
- A100 (current): ~80 tokens/sec per GPU (gen-heavy, small batches)
- H100: ~170–200 tokens/sec per GPU depending on quantization/batching (approx 2.1x median vs A100)
- L40S: ~120–150 tokens/sec per GPU but with better mem/density for large-context runs (approx 1.5x vs A100)

Perf-per-dollar: with committed pricing for reserved pools, H100 typically nets ~1.6–2.0x perf-per-dollar for throughput-first workloads because of higher effective token throughput and improved batch utilization. L40S can be the sweet spot if you need larger context windows and slightly lower cost per-card but lower peak throughput.

I've attached a short perf brief and an initial MAP. Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow 11/17 to review?

Thanks for the forward — adding a quick technical breakdown and recommendation. I ran targeted microbenchmarks against a representative 6B and 20B family model (seq len 512, batch sizes swept for latency). Key findings:

Summary numbers (median across runs):
- A100 (current): 70–85 tokens/sec per card (varies with batch); memory pressure on longer contexts leads to tail latency spikes.
- H100 (SXM): 160–200 tokens/sec per card (optimized kernels, better FP16/TF32 throughput). Tail latency improvements ~30–45% vs A100.
- L40S: 110–145 tokens/sec per card, but handles 2x context with less degradation (useful if you have many 2k+ context runs).

Perf-per-dollar note: when priced at reserved rates we modeled for RED-8942, H100 yields ~1.9x effective tokens/hour per dollar vs A100 for this workload. The main driver is improved batching efficiency and higher single-card throughput — you get fewer cards to meet throughput. L40S gives ~1.35x tokens/hour per dollar vs A100, but is attractive if the workload shifts to larger contexts (less swapping, fewer falls back to CPU).

Recommendation (practical):
1) For Stella's stated goal of p95 <250ms at 700 conc and throughput-heavy inference, prioritize H100 for the incremental capacity. It gives the cleanest perf-per-dollar uplift.
2) Offer a mixed-pool rollout: convert the 8 new cards to H100 and phase-migrate 4 of the existing A100s to L40S if they need more large-context runs — this keeps costs balanced and provides fallback options.
3) Commit Redwood to a throughput SLA for the expanded pool: guaranteed aggregate token throughput floor (e.g., 15k tokens/sec sustained, 21k tokens/sec burst with 2x autoretry) with SLA credits if we miss p95 targets, subject to mutually agreed telemetry and routing policy.

I'll attach the capacity_calc_20261118.csv and a condensed perf table.

—Priyom

- Pricing (committed reserved): Monthly reserved fee for +8 H100s: $94,000/mo (discounted reserved rate). Net impact vs current spend: ~+36% monthly commit, but perf-per-dollar improves ~1.8x effective tokens/dollar for baseline workloads.
